items.text: Sometimes the person who trusts God is abused and abandoned by family members. When things like that happen to us, we might be tempted to become angry with God. We might wonder, “What’s the point of trying to do the right thing if it only seems to make life harder?”

Joseph, the son of Jacob, could have wondered that. At times, this faithful man prospered; at other times, it seemed that the more faithful he was, the more hardship he faced. But Joseph never left the Lord, and the Lord never left Joseph.
That doesn’t mean the Lord prevented bad things from happening to Joseph, but through it all, “the Lord was with him” (Genesis 39:3). The Lord blesses people who trust Him and keep His commandments.

What do you learn from Joseph’s story that could help you recognize the Lord’s presence in your life? What evidence have you seen that the Lord has not forsaken you in times of trial? Consider how you can share your experiences with family members and future generations.

What can you do now to help ensure that these trials don’t pull you away from the Lord? Consider writing a letter to encourage your future self to stay close to Him no matter what. Include insights from Joseph’s life.

What can you learn from Joseph’s example when revelation seems difficult to understand? Ponder how the Lord is revealing His will to you. What are you doing to act on revelation He has given you? How are you seeking additional guidance from Him?

If Joseph were to give counsel on how to resist temptation to commit sexual sin, what do you think he would say? Joseph’s example can apply to other kinds of temptation. Consider making a plan for avoiding and resisting temptation.
Think about situations to avoid and how you will “flee” when the temptation arises. What do you learn from scriptures like Matthew 4:1–11 about how the Savior can help you resist temptation?
Think about times in the past when you successfully avoided or resisted temptation. How did the Savior help you? (see 2 Nephi 4:18–33). With the Lord’s help, you can flee temptation.

Joseph’s interpretation of dreams led to his rise to power and ultimately his ability to prepare Egypt for possible hardships. From his story, we learn that the Lord will help us prepare for difficult times if we remain faithful.
